context.analysis:
## Overview
[This hybrid system modernizes a regional insurer's claims platform by gradually migrating claim types from a legacy mainframe to Azure while maintaining seamless coexistence. It ensures zero data loss, strict security, and rapid rollback capabilities.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Business Operations Managers, Migration Admins
* Insurer Active Directory / Azure Entra ID, Legacy Payment Gateway
* Modern Claims Platform (Azure West Europe): Azure Web App, API Gateway, Anti-Corruption Layer
* Legacy Mainframe (On-Premises): COBOL/DB2 System of Record
* Integration Layer: Azure Service Bus

## Relationships
* Users to API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC and Azure Entra ID SSO
* Modern Claims Platform to Insurer Active Directory via OIDC
* Modern Claims Platform to Legacy Mainframe via Azure Service Bus using asynchronous messaging and encrypted payloads
* Hybrid traffic secured via site-to-site VPN or Azure ExpressRoute with mutual TLS (mTLS)

## Technology Stack
* Cloud Provider: Azure (West Europe region) and On-Premises Mainframe
* Authentication: Azure AD / Entra ID with OAuth 2.0 / OIDC for secure SSO and RBAC
* Integration & Routing: Azure Service Bus with Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) pattern to decouple lifecycles and protect the mainframe
* Security: Azure Key Vault for customer-managed keys (CMK), TLS 1.3, and mTLS for hybrid connectivity

## Rationale
* The hybrid architecture allows gradual claim-type migration while keeping the legacy mainframe as the system of record for 3 years.
* Asynchronous messaging via Azure Service Bus and the ACL pattern respect the strict batch window and the constraint of maximum one mainframe interface change per quarter.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous operations. Its core purpose is to migrate claim types incrementally via an Anti-Corruption Layer while ensuring zero data loss and unified user experiences.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Business Operations Managers, and Migration Admins
- Single Sign-On / Identity Provider: Azure Entra ID (Active Directory)
- Frontend: Angular/React Single Page Application hosted in Azure Static Web Apps
- API Gateway / Router: Azure API Management (APIM)
- Core Platform: Node.js/Java microservices on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
- Integration & ACL: Azure Service Bus
- Storage: Azure SQL Database
- Analytics: Azure Event Hubs, Stream Analytics, Azure Synapse Analytics, and Power BI Embedded
- Legacy System: On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe

## Relationships
- End Users to Azure Static Web Apps via HTTPS for UI access
- APIM to Azure Static Web Apps and AKS via HTTPS / REST APIs
- AKS to Azure SQL Database via TDS / SQL protocols
- AKS / APIM to Azure Service Bus via AMQP for asynchronous messaging
- Azure Service Bus / APIM to On-Premises Mainframe via mTLS over IPsec VPN / ExpressRoute
- AKS / Azure SQL to Azure Event Hubs via internal event streaming
- Business Operations Managers to Dashboard Container via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Hosts the SPA frontend for fast global delivery
- Azure API Management (APIM): Enforces OIDC/OAuth2 authentication and dynamic routing for claim-type migration
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS): Runs containerized microservices and backend-for-frontend (BFF) components
- Azure Service Bus: Provides reliable asynchronous messaging for the Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- Azure SQL Database: Stores modern claim types with encryption at rest (Customer-Managed Keys)
- Azure Event Hubs & Synapse Analytics: Ingests CDC streams and operational metrics for auditing and reporting
- Azure Entra ID: Handles Single Sign-On and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture uses an Anti-Corruption Layer and API Gateway to decouple modern cloud services from the legacy mainframe, satisfying the strict 3-year migration constraint and max one-per-quarter interface limit. It leverages Azure managed services to provide high availability, robust security via mTLS and zero-trust principles, and a one-day rollback capability without extending the rigid nightly batch window.]

Azure Static Web Apps.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance claims mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid cloud platform while ensuring uninterrupted legacy processing.]

## Key Elements
- Azure Static Web Apps (Angular/React SPA frontend)
- SPA Router & View Modules
- Auth & Session Manager
- API Proxy / Fallback
- Configuration & Feature Flag Service
- Telemetry Client
- Azure API Management (APIM)
- Azure Entra ID / Active Directory

## Relationships
- End Customers, Brokers, Claims Adjusters, Operations Managers, Migration Admins -> Azure Static Web Apps [HTTPS]
- SPA Router -> Auth & Session Manager [In-memory / HTTPS]
- SPA Router -> API Proxy [HTTPS]
- API Proxy -> Azure API Management [HTTPS / REST APIs]
- Auth & Session Manager -> Azure Entra ID [OAuth / OIDC]
- Telemetry Client -> Azure Application Insights [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps: Manages frontend hosting and global delivery to reduce operational overhead for a low-cloud-experience team.
- Angular/React: Powers dynamic single-page application interfaces and role-based routing.
- Azure Entra ID: Provides single sign-on (SSO) integration using built-in SWA authentication.
- Azure Application Insights: Tracks real-user metrics (RUM) and performance for adjuster screens.

## Rationale
[This architecture uses managed cloud services to minimize infrastructure complexity for an inexperienced team while providing robust security controls and gradual migration paths. It guarantees low-latency user interfaces and strict data protection without altering the core mainframe processing window.]

Azure API Management.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurance claims mainframe by gradually migrating claim types to a cloud platform. Azure API Management acts as the central hybrid routing and security gateway.]

## Key Elements
* Azure API Management (APIM) Container
* API Gateway Component (Edge proxy, JWT validation, rate-limiting)
* Policy Engine Component (XML dynamic routing, correlation ID injection)
* Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
* On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
* Azure Entra ID
* Azure Application Insights

## Relationships
* API Gateway Component -> Azure Kubernetes Service: Forwards modernized claim requests [HTTPS / REST]
* API Gateway Component -> On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Routes legacy traffic [mTLS over ExpressRoute / IPsec VPN]
* API Gateway Component -> Azure Entra ID: Validates OIDC/OAuth2 tokens [HTTPS / REST]
* Policy Engine Component -> Azure Application Insights: Streams sanitized telemetry and metrics [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Azure API Management (Internal VNet Mode): Manages hybrid routing and protects the legacy mainframe
* Azure Entra ID: Enforces Single Sign-On and OAuth2/OIDC JWT token validation
* Azure Key Vault: Manages certificate lifecycle and pinning for mainframe mTLS integration
* Azure Application Insights: Collects sanitized operational telemetry and business metrics

## Rationale
[This architecture uses Azure API Management in Internal VNet Mode to safely route traffic between modern microservices and the legacy mainframe. This design ensures seamless gradual migration and rapid one-day rollbacks while protecting sensitive data.]

Azure Kubernetes Service.analysis:
## Overview
[This system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe by deploying a hybrid cloud claims platform on Azure Kubernetes Service. It enables gradual claim type migration while maintaining seamless legacy integration and business continuity.]

## Key Elements
- Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
- API Gateway / BFF (Node.js)
- Claim Processing Domain Services (Java/Spring Boot)
- Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) Adapter
- ArgoCD (GitOps)
- Azure Service Bus
- Azure SQL Database

## Relationships
- Azure API Management -> API Gateway / BFF: Forwards requests [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway / BFF -> Claim Processing Domain Services: Internal communication [gRPC / HTTP/2]
- Claim Processing Domain Services -> Mainframe ACL Adapter: Asynchronous messaging [AMQP / AMQPS]
- Claim Processing Domain Services -> Azure SQL Database: Reads/writes modern data [TDS / SQL]
- Claim Processing Domain Services -> Azure Service Bus: Publishes and consumes events [AMQPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Kubernetes Service: Container orchestration runtime chosen for gradual claim migration capability.
- Node.js & Java/Spring Boot: Microservices runtime supporting BFF UI composition and CQRS domain services.
- ArgoCD: GitOps deployment engine enabling automated canary releases for low-experience cloud teams.
- Azure CNI & Network Policies: Implements strict microsegmentation and security boundaries.

## Rationale
[The architecture decouples legacy mainframe latency via CQRS and an Anti-Corruption Layer to meet performance goals. It balances the team's low cloud experience with robust security controls and zero-downtime migration pathways.]

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a modern hybrid cloud platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old insurance mainframe claims system while maintaining continuous processing. It enables online claim submissions and adjuster workflows while incrementally migrating claim types.]

## Key Elements
- **Azure Service Bus**: Central messaging broker providing reliable asynchronous integration via Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL)
- **Claim Migration Topic & Subscriptions**: Pub/sub engine with session-based ordering for incremental claim-type routing
- **Mainframe Sync Queue**: Partitioned, transactional queue with duplicate detection for guaranteed consistency
- **Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ)**: Automated capture mechanism for poisoned messages and batch window lockouts
- **Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)**: Host for Node.js/Java microservices interacting with the bus

## Relationships
- **Azure Kubernetes Service -> Azure Service Bus**: Publishes and consumes asynchronous messages using AMQP 1.0 over TLS 1.3
- **Azure API Management -> Azure Service Bus**: Sends asynchronous integration messages via AMQP 1.0
- **Azure Service Bus -> On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe**: Communicates legacy synchronization via mTLS over IPsec VPN / ExpressRoute

## Technology Stack
- **Azure Service Bus**: Selected for reliable transactional messaging and enterprise decoupling
- **AMQP 1.0**: Protocol for connection multiplexing and enterprise-grade reliability over hybrid boundaries
- **Azure Entra ID (Managed Identities)**: Replaces SAS connection strings to enforce least-privilege RBAC
- **Terraform**: Infrastructure-as-Code tool used to manage cloud components and prevent configuration drift

## Rationale
[This architecture successfully decouples high-performance cloud UI requirements from slow mainframe responses while ensuring zero data loss during incremental migration. It securely bridges the hybrid environment using robust message queuing and strict identity controls.]

Azure SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
This system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining legacy synchronization.

## Key Elements
* Azure SQL Database
* Claim Transactional Store
* Integration Staging Store
* Row-Level Security & Access Management
* Azure Kubernetes Service
* Legacy Mainframe (On-Premises)
* Microsoft Entra ID
* Azure Private Endpoints

## Relationships
* Azure Kubernetes Service -> Claim Transactional Store: Executes parameterized SQL queries via TDS / SQL over TLS 1.3
* Claim Transactional Store -> Microsoft Entra ID: Authenticates requests using managed identities
* Integration Staging Store -> Legacy Mainframe (On-Premises): Syncs delta changes asynchronously via Change Data Capture (CDC) and data connectors
* Claim Transactional Store -> Azure SQL Database-Level Auditing: Writes security logs to Azure Storage/Log Analytics

## Technology Stack
* Azure SQL Database: Chosen for built-in High Availability and managed service benefits given limited cloud experience
* Temporal Tables (System-Versioned): Selected to track historical changes and satisfy auditability requirements
* Change Data Capture (CDC): Implemented to support the one-day rollback constraint (R-06)
* Microsoft Entra ID: Enforced for single sign-on (R-07) and secure database authentication
* Azure Private Endpoints: Deployed to isolate the database in a private subnet and prevent public access

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture balances low cloud team experience with strict consistency and rollback requirements. Leveraging native Azure SQL features minimizes custom code while ensuring secure coexistence with the legacy mainframe.

Analytics Platform.analysis:
## Overview
[The Analytics Platform provides real-time reporting, auditing, and migration tracking for the modern insurance claims system. It ensures business continuity by monitoring dual-system performance during the three-year mainframe migration.]

## Key Elements
* Business Operations Managers and Claims Executives
* Azure Event Hubs
* Azure Stream Analytics
* Azure Synapse Analytics (Dedicated SQL Pool)
* Power BI Embedded
* Azure Functions
* Azure Key Vault and Log Analytics

## Relationships
* Azure Kubernetes Service / Azure SQL Database -> Azure Event Hubs [AMQP over TLS 1.3]
* Azure Functions -> Azure Synapse Analytics [T-SQL via TDS/TLS 1.3]
* Azure Synapse Analytics -> Power BI Embedded [Direct Query / HTTPS via TLS 1.3]
* Analytics Platform -> Azure Key Vault [Managed Identity / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Event Hubs: Ingests real-time CDC streams using AMQP for high throughput
* Azure Stream Analytics: Processes in-transit validation checks to satisfy R-04
* Azure Synapse Analytics: Stores historical claim metrics with Row-Level Security and dynamic data masking
* Power BI Embedded: Renders the Migration Executive Dashboard with Azure Entra ID SSO
* Azure Functions: Executes serverless reconciliation logic without custom ETL infrastructure

## Rationale
[This managed-service-heavy architecture minimizes custom code to accommodate the team's low cloud experience. It provides secure, real-time visibility to satisfy strict auditability and compliance requirements during the hybrid migration.]
